scope: Company invitation redemption, selected company session context, primary account role preservation; no commits, push, deploy, dependencies or schema migration.
acceptanceCriteria: Legacy /auth/signup?invite links redirect to the invitation page; login, signup, MFA and email verification preserve a safe internal invitation destination.
Signed-in active user must have a verified email equal to the invitation email, case-insensitively.
Acceptance updates exactly one invited membership and marks the invite accepted in one PostgreSQL transaction, with expiry checked at the final claim.
No primary users.role changes, no new company, no duplicate memberships or invitation ownership/capability escalation.
Company context selection is bound to the current user live session and refresh credential, with current active company membership and company organization type.
Company API, session reload and refresh enforce current membership and type; removed/suspended selected context never silently falls back.
Company context cannot authorize partner/mechanic APIs; explicit exit restores primary account context.
Team role/capability edits preserve primary account role and cannot exceed the acting member rights.

contracts.GET /api/auth/company-invitations/:token: requireAuth, matching current email. Returns invitation {organizationId,companyName,role,status,expiresAt}. No token/email/inviter data in response.
contracts.POST /api/auth/company-invitations/:toke: requireAuth, authLimiter. Returns {ok:true,organization:{id,name,type}}. No new login session and no changed primary role.
contracts.GET /api/auth/company-contexts: requireAuth. Returns {organizations:[{id,name}]} for active company memberships/ownership.
contracts.POST /api/auth/company-context: requireAuth and live same-user session + refreshToken. Body {organizationId:string|null,refreshToken}; null explicitly resets to primary account default context. Returns {user,accessToken,refreshToken}. Same durable session and raw credential; signed selected org claims only.
contracts.SessionUser: role remains primary role. Additive organizationId,organizationType,organizationRole authorize UI context; all APIs re-read DB membership/status/permissions.

impact: Company endpoints now use selected company context instead of primary account role. Existing requirePermission gates continue to govern mutations and current DB memberships govern all company reads.
Default organization selection is constrained to matching primary organization type; selected secondary company context is explicit and signed, compatible with legacy default refresh tokens.
Suspending/deleting membership immediately invalidates company API access and refresh; duplicate legacy user memberships in a company are denied until corrected.
Company joining does not create organizations, wallets, billing subscriptions or duplicate users; all existing financial service flows remain under their permission gates.
Root hardened customer personal wallet lookups independently to force personal scope while company context is selected.

Only partner router uses requireOrgMembership; it now rejects company context even for a preserved partner/mechanic primary role. Legacy minimal test fixtures must include real org type and signed orgType.
Pending team role edits synchronize invite.role; team removal revokes matching pending invites so old links cannot revive a deleted membership.
recovery: Database failure during membership activation, invitation claim or audit rolls back all changes; tested with forced audit error and successful retry.
If acceptance commits but context selection/network fails, the accepted invitation page offers Open company dashboard and retries selection without replaying acceptance.
Expired or revoked links require a new invitation. Owners can remove the invited team row and invite again through existing team workflow.
Explicit Return to primary account requests a default signed context reset before navigation; logout invalidates the existing durable session and clears local session state.
No migration required; rollback affects application routes/helpers only. Existing accepted memberships remain valid persisted records if application code is rolled back.
limitationsAndReleaseGates: Root owns browser verification and full integrated suites; this agent did not inspect rendered desktop/mobile UI or conduct independent release review.
Qualified human review of authentication/tenant boundaries is required before production release. No security or production-readiness guarantee made.
Live invitation email provider delivery not exercised; isolated tests prohibit external network. Existing mailer delivery path retained with awaited emailDelivered response.
Legacy invitations require their existing invited membership row. Deleted, suspended, conflicting or duplicate legacy rows are deliberately rejected instead of inferred/repaired.

Invitation tokens retain the existing opaque plaintext token schema; 192-bit generated random values, authenticated preview, email verification/binding, expiry and auth rate limiter apply. No schema expansion requested.
Selected context refresh JWT expiry uses the existing signer policy and durable session expires_at cap; any pre-existing remember-me JWT-vs-session TTL mismatch is unchanged by this task.
Invitation manager/dispatcher roles retain existing explicit capability behavior; membership role is not assumed to imply privileges beyond existing owner/admin bypass.
Root writes the single Edirae Learn breakdown and index after integration; this agent did not add a duplicate breakdown.

All ten local UI reference catalog summaries consulted; existing green/navy tokens and semantic form controls kept. Focused Better Design typography and taste-accessibility/code craft references inspected. No hosted design service, paid account, external project upload or new UI dependency used.
